title: Conduct That Doesn’t Fit
note: He defines this as evil conduct that doesn’t fit austerity: lacking strength, someone wants again the pleasures of desire they gave up, yet keeps the garb. It follows austerity in order to forbid this.

couplets.plain: The five elements laugh to themselves at the hidden conduct of a deceitful mind.
couplets.pm: The five elements that make up a deceiver’s body see their hidden conduct and laugh among themselves. Desire troubles this person, who denies it and deceives others. The elements witness all that thieves do unseen, so they know the conduct and how it is hidden. A fault can’t stay hidden, so such conduct won’t do.

links.quote: laugh to themselves at the hidden conduct

couplets.plain: What use is a look as high as the sky if your own heart sinks into what you know is a fault?
couplets.pm: What use is the garb of austerity, high as the sky, if your heart sinks into what you know to be a fault? A fault done knowingly can’t be washed away, so the heart stays at fault. Then the garb is good only for frightening others.

links.quote: a look as high as the sky

couplets.plain: The strong look of someone with no strength is like a cow wearing a tiger’s skin to graze.
couplets.pm: Someone without the strength to rule his mind takes the garb of the strong and follows the mind. That is like a cow grazing crops under a tiger’s skin, unchased by the watchmen. Having left his own wife, unsuspected, he goes after women who belong to others, as the cow leaves its own grass for others’ crops.

links.quote: a cow wearing a tiger’s skin
links.reason: Someone with no strength looks fierce but is only a cow inside a tiger’s skin.

couplets.plain: To hide behind austerity and do wrong is like a hunter hiding in a bush to snare birds.
couplets.pm: Such a person, hiding in the garb of austerity and doing what isn’t austerity, is like a hunter hiding in a bush to trap birds. Doing what isn’t austerity means bringing women who belong to others under his power.

links.quote: hide behind austerity and do wrong
links.reason: Austerity is a hunter’s bush, cover from which to do wrong.

couplets.plain: The hidden conduct of those who say “We are free of attachment” brings many troubles, until they cry “What have we done?”
couplets.pm: Some say “We are free of attachment” so that others will respect them. Their hidden conduct seems sweet at the time, but later brings many sufferings, until they cry “What have we done?” For a small pleasure that dies in a moment, they do a great and lasting sin.

links.quote: until they cry “What have we done?”
links.reason: The boast of having no attachments ends in the cry of “What have we done?”

couplets.plain: No one is crueller than those who don’t renounce in their hearts but live by deceit, as if they had renounced.
couplets.pm: No one in the world is crueller than those who keep attachment in the heart, pose as renouncers and live by deceiving those who give to them. People give in hope of becoming gods, and taking those gifts brings the givers low birth instead. So these deceivers harm those who do them good.

links.quote: live by deceit, as if they had renounced

couplets.plain: The world holds people red outside like the crab’s-eye seed, yet black inside, like its tip.
couplets.pm: The world has people who in their garb are red like the outside of that seed, yet whose minds are dark like its tip. Red and black here pass from colour to uprightness and ignorance, so the likeness is one of quality.

links.quote: red outside like the crab’s-eye seed, yet black inside
links.reason: The two-coloured crab’s-eye seed stands for people red outside and black within.

couplets.plain: Many people, the stain still in their minds, bathe to look worthy and live in hiding behind it.
couplets.pm: Many in the world, with stain in their minds, plunge into water to show that austerity has made them worthy, and hide in that act. The stain is desire, anger and delusion. They bathe not to lose these but to be thought worthy. Some read மாண்டார் நீராடி as “having the nature of the worthy”.

links.quote: the stain still in their minds
links.reason: Bathing to look worthy leaves the stain in the mind as it was.

couplets.plain: An arrow is cruel, a bent harp is true. Judge people the same way, by what they do.
couplets.pm: An arrow is straight in shape but cruel in act. The harp is bent at the neck but straight in act. Judge those who do austerity likewise, by what they do and not by their form. The arrow’s act is killing, the harp’s is giving pleasure with music. If the act is sin, call them cruel. If it is righteous, upright.

links.quote: Judge people the same way, by what they do
Judge people the same way, by what they do

couplets.plain: No need for shaving or growing long hair, if you give up what the world condemns.
couplets.pm: Those who do austerity need no garb of shaved heads or matted hair, if they give up the conduct that the high have condemned as unfit for austerity. Plucking the hair counts as shaving. Those free of false conduct need no garb at all.

links.quote: give up what the world condemns
